text:
maria: Hey team, seeing a sustained p99 latency spike (~120ms -> 600ms) on serving nodes under long-context workloads. Correlation looks tied to KV cache churn when the system hits paging thresholds.
ajay: ugh, I saw that in the dashboard too this morning. Which eviction policy was in use on affected hosts? FIFO or LRU?
derek: FIFO pools for those instances (reserved for certain burst configs). I pulled a brief flamegraph — the spin is around eviction bookkeeping + reinsert path.
maria: here's a tiny snippet from the logs around the spike:
```
[2026-11-02T09:14:23Z] kv_evict: candidates=512 current_mem=78% evicted=128 policy=FIFO
[2026-11-02T09:14:23Z] kv_reinsert: key=0x7fffa3 reuse=false slot_mismatch=true
[2026-11-02T09:14:23Z] kv_pager: page_in=0 page_out=3 backlog=42
```
ajay: slot_mismatch=true stands out — suggests fragmentation/tombstone chain where reinsert can't reuse slot and triggers extra allocations. That plus FIFO ordering could be thrashing.
sophie: we saw something similar in the long-context perf test where KV chains grew and then reinsert became O(chain_length). I pushed a small profiler patch yesterday: https://git.internal/r/redwood/serve/commit/abc1234 — might help capture stack traces for these paths.
maria: thanks @sophie — can you enable it on one of the affected canaries? I want to verify whether evicted entries are being mistakenly considered non-evictable on reinsert which would flip pressure back on the pager.
sophie: enabled on canary-4. logs now show a repeating pattern: evict->reinsert->evict with slightly different eviction candidates each cycle. Looks like FIFO's head moves but reuse is failing, so we keep cycling.
derek: that matches a correctness hypothesis: FIFO evict picks oldest slots, but if we have variable-size fragment groups and tombstones, LRU's recency info might have avoided the churn. Worth comparing.
ajay: quick repro command for local: `./bench_kv --policy=fifo --workers=48 --long_context=128k --pressure=steady` — I can run a pairwise compare.
maria: run both FIFO and LRU and dump kv metrics at 1s resolution. We need: evicted_count, reinsert_failures, avg_chain_len, pager_ops/sec, p99 latency.
sophie: initial local run (FIFO) shows: evicted_count=14k reinsert_failures=620 avg_chain_len=4.8 pager_ops=78/s p99=420ms. LRU run: evicted=13k reinsert_failures=12 avg_chain_len=1.2 pager_ops=9/s p99=110ms.
ajay: wow that gap is huge. So FIFO seems to be exposing fragmentation + reuse failure which multiplies pager traffic.
derek: possible causes: race in marking slot used vs tombstone GC, or FIFO pointer wrap/overflow bug under high churn. Also check atomic CAS ordering in reinsert path (we moved from compare_exchange to weaker primitives in #4421).
maria: @derek can you bisect around #4421? If the weaker CAS change regresses correctness under concurrency, that'd explain reinsert false negatives.
derek: starting a bisect now. initial suspicion: commit 9f4e2b6 changed the reinsert fast-path to rely on relaxed ordering.
sophie: while bisect runs, we should mitigate: 1) fallback policy: prefer LRU on high-density nodes (config flag), 2) increase tombstone GC frequency, 3) add a short reinsert backoff to avoid hot loop.
ajay: I'll prototype a dynamic policy switch via metric trigger (pager_ops/sec > 50 => switch to LRU for 30s). Should be low-risk.
maria: good. also add additional tracing for 'slot_mismatch' to include slot index and last_seen_seq so we can see if CAS mismatch is timing or logical.
derek: bisect result: regression introduced in 9f4e2b6 (relaxed CAS) — reproducer fails when core_count >= 24 and sustained reinsert rate > 5k/s. Fix candidate: revert relaxed CAS or add explicit acquire-release pair on success.
sophie: opened PR #4508 with acquire-release variant and extra unit tests for racing reinserts. Also toggled canary-4 to LRU as temporary mitigation.
ops-bot: deploy started for canary-4 (PR #4508) by sophie at 2026-11-02T10:22:11Z :rocket:
maria: after canary deploy metrics: FIFO nodes dropped p99 by ~30% but still > target. LRU canary is back to baseline.
ajay: we should also audit our eviction heuristics: FIFO is simple but interacts poorly with fragmentation. Maybe keep FIFO for tiny entries and LRU for large KV groups.
derek: agreed. I'll draft an RFC for a hybrid eviction policy: size-aware LRU windows + FIFO fast lane for tiny cold keys.
sophie: adding test jobs that simulate long-context generations to the CI perf suite, and I'll instrument the e2e harness to assert max pager_ops/sec under steady state.
maria: thanks all. Action items: derek bisect + RFC, sophie PR and canary rollout, ajay metric-triggered fallback, i’ll follow up with postmortem if degraded for >1h. :thumbsup:
ajay: noted, I'll post the bench scripts and raw traces to the perf channel after today's runs. :mag:
